items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: And previous to that, Ben Webster came through with Duke Ellington, and he had been listening to Charlie Parker lately, and he was very impressed. And he came down to the club and he sat down and played piano with us

ctx.x: first time I've seen somebody play that small amount and get complete response from the audience. That was really something special. I'll always remember that scene, you know.

Anyway, back to Tweed(?) Beard. We were working a little place out on Grand River, a little dance hall out there, a bar. And he had just hired a saxophone player from...was it Saginaw...anyway, one of those little towns up in Michigan -- and that was George Nicholson, a tenor player, his first time away from home. [LAUGHS HEARTILY] And he was playing good. He had Ben Webster on his mind, you know.

And this was during the period with Ben Webster, and all the alto players mostly had their minds on Charlie Parker... Like, Sonny Stitt hadn't heard Charlie Parker yet. He was playing strictly out of the Benny Carter bag, and Wardell was playing out of the Benny Carter bag, and Bernie Peacock -- they was all working out of Benny Carter's bag. And one period there when Benny Carter was out here, working at the Club Alabam, you could get him faintly on the radio late at night in Detroit -- get him faintly, boy. And…
